source_verification_receipts.locator: Theorem 1 and Appendix B, proof of Theorem 1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper defines CRTs through a partition of the assignment space and proves validity through the conditional probability-integral-transform argument.

Validity for arbitrary permutation distributions is obtained with an independent draw sigma_0 from q and comparisons transformed by sigma composed with sigma_0 inverse; the paper does not characterize fixed deterministic row kernels.
Theorem 4 constructs finite-sample quantile confidence sets under exchangeable assignment; simultaneous all-quantile inference is separately established in Section 5.5.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2208.11798v3, 9 May 2023; corroborating preprint because the cited Biometrika version was inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies independent strata with within-stratum exchangeable assignments, obtains valid quantile-null p-values, reduces computation to multiple-choice knapsack instances, and gives simultaneous inversion.
The method represents a null through a unit-by-assignment bipartite graph and uses bicliques to obtain sharp conditional randomization tests under general interference.

The paper improves biclique testing through a power evaluation and a refined selection procedure, rather than globally optimizing exact rejection probability over arbitrary valid state-dependent row kernels.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2308.00202, latest public preprint; unpublished non-archival WIP
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops conditional randomization tests for heterogeneous effects under network interference and reports validity for its conditioning procedure; it is not a published exact network individual-effect-quantile optimizer.

The article improves randomization-based inference for distributions and quantiles of individual treatment effects in completely randomized, stratified, sampling-based, and matched experiments, without a network-interference coupled-schedule result.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Correct the Caughey comparator anchor: cite Theorem 4 for individual quantile intervals and Section 5.5 for simultaneity; add Chen and Li (2026) and state precisely why its no-interference improvement is orthogonal to the coupled-network kernel.

Define the exact rank-score class, monotonicity, and tie-breaking rule for the two no-interference reductions, then state separate reduction clauses matching Caughey and Su–Li rather than an undefined generic distribution-free statistic.

Promote the directed-cycle separation into a generic directed-support criterion or family of supports with a certified positive partition gap, so the design result is not carried mainly by one three-state witness.
